title: Incident
description: One publicly reported security incident affecting an organization. Small on purpose: every field must be fillable from public text, and 'unknown' is always allowed.

id.description: sha1 of normalized org_name + the first disclosed_date. Permanent: later sources for the same incident attach to this id (pipeline merge window), so it is the handle for corrections.

schema_version.description: 1.2 added attack_techniques, org_id, letter, sources[].date. 1.1 added actor, third_party, cve, entry_asset, control_failure, credential_source, data_types, discovered_date, ransomware. Bump the minor on additive enum changes, the major on anything that breaks comparability. Log every change in docs/CHANGELOG.md.

org_type.description: Coarse sector. Maps roughly onto VERIS victim.industry at the 2-digit NAICS level; kept to ~12 buckets so counts are meaningful.

disclosed_date.description: Date the incident became public (filing date, notice date, article date). Always known.

incident_date.description: Date the intrusion began or was discovered, if stated. Null if not stated.

discovered_date.description: When the organization discovered it, if stated. With incident_date this gives dwell time.

initial_access.description: How the attacker (or error) got in. Aligned to ATT&CK Initial Access (TA0001) plus non-attack causes. 'unknown' is the expected value for most regulator-only records.

initial_access_attack_id.description: ATT&CK technique ID if one clearly applies (e.g. T1566, T1078, T1190, T1195, T1133). Null otherwise.

veris_action.description: VERIS action category, for comparability with DBIR.

entry_asset.description: The asset the attacker came in through (VERIS action.hacking.vector, collapsed). Only if stated.

control_failure.description: Why the attack worked: the control that was missing or weak, only if the source states it. Requires supporting_quote. Distinct from initial_access (how they got in).

credential_source.description: Where the credentials came from, when initial_access is stolen_or_valid_credentials. Null otherwise.

cve.description: CVE ids named in the source as exploited. Checked verbatim against the text.

root_cause.description: One plain sentence on the underlying weakness, only if the source states or clearly implies it (e.g. 'Long-lived OAuth token for a third-party integration was not rotated after a prior compromise'). Null if the source doesn't say.

attack_techniques.description: Every ATT&CK technique the text states (initial access, collection, exfiltration, impact). Kept only when the text carries the behaviour's words (extract.TECHNIQUE_TRIGGERS); initial_access_attack_id and ransomware=true are added deterministically.

technology_involved.description: Named vendors, products or categories that were the point of entry or the system breached (e.g. 'Salesforce', 'Okta SSO', 'GitHub Actions', 'Citrix NetScaler', 'VPN appliance', 'email'). Empty if none named.

third_party.description: DBIR's three archetypes. Separate from initial_access, which stays the mechanism: a vendor's unpatched product is exploit_public_facing_app + vendor_product; a stolen vendor OAuth token is stolen_or_valid_credentials + vendor_connection.

involved.description: true if a third party was part of how it happened; null if not stated.

archetype.description: vendor_product: flaw or backdoor in a vendor product in the victim's own environment. vendor_hosted_data: the vendor held the data and was breached, or the victim's account on the vendor was abused. vendor_connection: the vendor's access or credentials into the victim were used.

actor.description: Who did it, VERIS-style. category/variety/motive only when the text says or the group is known (pipeline/actors.py); name only if the text attributes or the group claims it.

name.description: Group or person as named in the source, e.g. 'ShinyHunters', 'Qilin'.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 of the actor's origin, only if stated.

ransomware.description: Ransomware or extortion was part of it. Null if not stated. impact_type says what happened; this says whether it was extortion.

data_types.description: VERIS data varieties, collapsed. Free from Maine notices and VCDB; from text only when stated.

records_affected.description: Individuals or records affected, only if a number is stated. Null otherwise. Never estimate.

evidence_level.description: Strongest form of evidence among the sources. Order: org_confirmed > regulator_filing > press_report > actor_claimed.

confidence.description: Extractor's confidence that initial_access and root_cause are supported by the text.

supporting_quote.description: Verbatim sentence from the source that supports initial_access / root_cause. Required when initial_access != unknown. Used for spot-checking hallucination.

summary.description: One neutral sentence: who, what was accessed, how (if known).

date.description: Date this source appeared, when known (a leak-site claim's post date).

reviewed.description: True once a human has checked the record. Unreviewed records are shown with a flag on the site.

first_seen.description: Run date on which this record entered the store. Survives merges; extracted_by.run_date does not.

org_id.description: Stable organization key (pipeline/orgs.py): hash of the canonical name after alias mapping.

letter.description: Notification letter read for this record (pipeline/letters.py).

updated_at.description: Last run date on which a later source changed this record (new source, richer fields, or an attached claim).

imported_from.description: Set on records imported from an existing coded dataset rather than extracted here. Keeps provenance and license obligations attached to the record.
